questions.stem: A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed $v_0$ and an angle $\theta$. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?

options.explanation: At maximum height, only the horizontal component of velocity remains; $v_0$ is incorrect as it is the initial speed.
Correct because at maximum height, the vertical component is zero, and only the horizontal component ($v_0 \cos \theta$) remains.
Incorrect because $v_0 \sin \theta$ represents the initial vertical component, which is zero at maximum height.
Incorrect because the horizontal speed (not zero) remains at maximum height.

2.  A spaceship is traveling with an initial velocity of 𝑣⃗ = (20.1 𝑚/𝑠)𝑖̂ when its rockets 
0
fire, imparting an acceleration of 𝑎⃗ = (2.02𝑚⁄𝑠2)𝑖̂+(4.03𝑚⁄𝑠2)𝑗̂. Based on this 
scenario, which of the following statements is correct? 
A.  The x-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant. 
B.  The y-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant. 
C. Both the direction of motion and speed change. 
D.  None of the above is correct.
questions.stem: A spaceship is traveling with an initial velocity of $\vec{v}_0 = (20.1 \text{ m/s})\hat{i}$ when its rockets fire, imparting an acceleration of $\vec{a} = (2.02 \text{ m/s}^2)\hat{i}+(4.03 \text{ m/s}^2)\hat{j}$. Based on this scenario, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The x-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant.
options.explanation: Incorrect because there is an acceleration in the x-direction, so the velocity changes.

options.text: The y-component of the spaceship’s velocity remains constant.
options.explanation: Incorrect because there is an acceleration in the y-direction, so the velocity changes.

options.text: Both the direction of motion and speed change.
options.explanation: Correct because there is acceleration in both directions, causing changes in both speed and direction.

options.text: None of the above is correct.
options.explanation: Incorrect because option C accurately describes what happens.
